source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

06091.t:
Sierra County barely moved in the race for governor. Hilton (R) carried it 929 to 570 over Becerra (D), a margin of 24 points, almost exactly Trump's 24-point margin in 2024. The shift toward the Democrats rounds to zero, while California as a whole moved 10 points their way and the typical county in the state moved 6. Sierra ranks 54th of California's 58 counties by move and 57th by votes cast. Similar Republican-leaning counties moved further: Colusa by 17 points, Yuba by 10 and Mariposa by 3.

Turnout was 1,499 votes, 85% of the 1,754 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, these figures are close to final.

06041.t:
Marin County gave Becerra (D) a 59-point lead over Hilton (R) for governor, 54,621 votes to 14,019. That is 5 points less Democratic than Harris's 64-point margin in 2024. It was the only shift of that size in California, where 54 of 58 counties moved left and the typical county moved 6 points toward the Democrats. Marin ranked last of the 58 by move. Nearby San Francisco and Santa Cruz each moved about 4 points left, while San Mateo moved 2 points right.

Only 52% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 68,640 votes so far are 48% of the 2024 total. With turnout this far down, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

The county moved less than a point toward the Democrats, while California as a whole moved 10 points and its typical county about 6. Calaveras ranks 51st of 58 counties by move. Among similar counties, Amador did not move at all, while Sutter moved 17 points and Yuba 10.

Turnout was 21,063 votes, 80% of the 26,479 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With just under 95% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

That 17-point move toward the Democrats ranks sixth of California's 58 counties, well beyond the typical county's 6 points and the state's 10. Similar counties moved by similar amounts: Kern 20 points, Madera 17, Kings 17.

Only 54% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The votes so far equal 56% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

Fifty-four moved left, the typical one by 6 points, and Becerra carried the state by 30 points, 10 better than Harris.

Comparable counties moved much further: Stanislaus swung 17 points left to a Democratic win, Tulare 17 points and Placer 3. Only 85% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 79,759 votes so far equal 71% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.
